lean.statement:
∀ {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ),
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let diagonalValue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
      (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
    let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) * Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    A.det = ∏ i : Fin d, diagonalValue i
approved_definition_context: Fin d is the finite coordinate set with natural values zero through d-1. The notation ∏ i : Fin d, f i is the ordinary finite product containing one factor for every coordinate.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) real is the full real orthogonal group. Its carrier requires both products with the transpose to equal identity, and permits either determinant sign. It supplies no probability law, determinant-one filter or algorithmic access.

Matrix.diagonal f is the actual square diagonal matrix with entries f i and zero off the diagonal. Matrix multiplication and transpose are ordinary finite-coordinate operations. The displayed local matrix is constructed from the displayed values and the actual orthogonal element.

Matrix.det is the genuine finite square determinant over real entries, defined by the alternating multilinear/Leibniz determinant. It is not trace, absolute determinant, a determinant sign, an assumed product or a supplied eigenvalue certificate. Equality is equality of real numbers.

Real.pi and Real.cos have their usual real meanings. The casts of the index value and dimension are real; the one-half and grid division are real operations. Division is totalized at zero, while the explicit dimension restriction separately makes its displayed denominator nonzero. All local lets and the conclusion share the same dimension, parameter and orthogonal element.
